title: 02. Ingestion & Chunking: Hierarchical Chunking (Parent-Child Chunks)
summary: Hierarchical chunking creates a two-level chunk structure: large parent chunks (1024-4096 tokens) that preserve broad context, and small child chunks (128-512 tokens) derived from the parents.

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body: Hierarchical chunking creates a two-level chunk structure: **large parent chunks** (1024-4096 tokens) that preserve broad context, and **small child chunks** (128-512 tokens) derived from the parents. During retrieval, the system searches over the small child chunks (for precision — small chunks are more specific and match queries better), but then returns the parent chunk (for context — the LLM needs broad context to answer well). This elegantly solves the precision-recall tradeoff in chunking: small chunks improve retrieval precision; large chunks improve generation quality. LangChain implements this as `ParentDocumentRetriever`.

diagrams.title: Parent-child chunking: search small, return big
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TB
  P["Parent chunk — full section, about 2000 tokens"] --> C1["child — 200 tokens"]
  P --> C2["child — 200 tokens"]
  P --> C3["child — 200 tokens"]
  Q["query"] -. "matches precisely" .-> C2
  C2 -- "return its parent to the LLM" --> P
diagrams.explain: Small chunks embed **precisely** (one idea each), large chunks give the LLM **enough context**. Parent-child chunking gets both: index the small children, and when a child matches, send its parent section to the model.

sections.title: ② Key Code
sections.body:
```python
from langchain.retrievers import ParentDocumentRetriever
from langchain.storage import InMemoryStore
from langchain_community.vectorstores import Chroma
from langchain_openai import OpenAIEmbeddings
from langchain_text_splitters import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
from langchain_core.documents import Document

def build_hierarchical_rag(documents: list[Document]):
    """
    Build a two-level hierarchical RAG system.
    
    Architecture:
    - Small chunks (256 tokens) are embedded and indexed for precision retrieval
    - When small chunk is retrieved, its parent (1024 tokens) is returned for context
    """
    # Child splitter: small for precise retrieval
    child_splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
        chunk_size=256,
        chunk_overlap=32,
    )
    
    # Parent splitter: large for rich context
    parent_splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
        chunk_size=1024,
        chunk_overlap=128,
    )
    
    # Vector store: indexes CHILD chunks (for search)
    embeddings = OpenAIEmbeddings(model="text-embedding-3-small")
    vectorstore = Chroma(
        collection_name="child_chunks",
        embedding_function=embeddings,
    )
    
    # Document store: stores PARENT chunks (for retrieval)
    parent_store = InMemoryStore()  # In production: use Redis or DynamoDB
    
    # Build retriever
    retriever = ParentDocumentRetriever(
        vectorstore=vectorstore,
        docstore=parent_store,
        child_splitter=child_splitter,
        parent_splitter=parent_splitter,
    )
    
    # Index documents (creates both parent and child chunks)
    retriever.add_documents(documents)
    
    return retriever

# Custom hierarchical chunking with three levels
class ThreeLevelChunker:
    """
    Document → Sections → Paragraphs → Sentences
    Retrieval on sentences, context from paragraphs, LLM sees sections.
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.section_splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
            chunk_size=4096, chunk_overlap=256,
            separators=["\n## ", "\n### ", "\n\n"]
        )
        self.para_splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
            chunk_size=1024, chunk_overlap=128,
            separators=["\n\n", "\n", ". "]
        )
        self.sent_splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
            chunk_size=256, chunk_overlap=32,
            separators=[". ", "? ", "! ", " "]
        )
    
    def build_hierarchy(self, docs: list[Document]) -> dict:
        """Build three-level chunk hierarchy with parent-child links."""
        sections = self.section_splitter.split_documents(docs)
        
        hierarchy = {}
        for i, section in enumerate(sections):
            section_id = f"section_{i}"
            section.metadata["chunk_id"] = section_id
            section.metadata["level"] = "section"
            
            paragraphs = self.para_splitter.split_documents([section])
            for j, para in enumerate(paragraphs):
                para_id = f"{section_id}_para_{j}"
                para.metadata["chunk_id"] = para_id
                para.metadata["parent_id"] = section_id
                para.metadata["level"] = "paragraph"
                
                sentences = self.sent_splitter.split_documents([para])
                for k, sent in enumerate(sentences):
                    sent_id = f"{para_id}_sent_{k}"
                    sent.metadata["chunk_id"] = sent_id
                    sent.metadata["parent_id"] = para_id
                    sent.metadata["grandparent_id"] = section_id
                    sent.metadata["level"] = "sentence"
            
            hierarchy[section_id] = {
                "section": section,
                "paragraphs": paragraphs,
                "sentences": [s for p in paragraphs 
                              for s in self.sent_splitter.split_documents([p])]
            }
        
        return hierarchy
```

sections.title: ④ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
HIERARCHICAL (PARENT-CHILD) CHUNKING
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

DOCUMENT STRUCTURE:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DOCUMENT (10,000 tokens)
  │
  ├─ PARENT CHUNK 1 (1024 tokens): "Section 1: Warranty Policy..."
  │    ├─ CHILD CHUNK 1a (256 tokens): "Warranty covers defects..."
  │    ├─ CHILD CHUNK 1b (256 tokens): "Coverage period is 2 years..."
  │    └─ CHILD CHUNK 1c (256 tokens): "Exclusions include accidental..."
  │
  ├─ PARENT CHUNK 2 (1024 tokens): "Section 2: Return Policy..."
  │    ├─ CHILD CHUNK 2a (256 tokens): "Returns accepted within 30..."
  │    ├─ CHILD CHUNK 2b (256 tokens): "Items must be in original..."
  │    └─ CHILD CHUNK 2c (256 tokens): "Contact support to initiate..."
  └─ ...

RETRIEVAL FLOW:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Query: "Is physical damage covered by warranty?"

Step 1: VECTOR SEARCH over CHILD CHUNKS (256 tokens)
  Match: CHILD CHUNK 1c "Exclusions include accidental damage and physical damage..."
  Score: 0.94 ← very precise match (small chunks are specific)

Step 2: LOOK UP PARENT
  CHILD 1c → parent_id = "PARENT CHUNK 1"
  Retrieve PARENT CHUNK 1 (1024 tokens):
  "Section 1: Warranty Policy. The warranty covers manufacturing defects
   for 2 years from date of purchase. Coverage applies to defects in
   materials and workmanship. Exclusions include accidental damage and
   physical damage caused by misuse..."
  
  ← Full section context preserved for LLM

Step 3: LLM GENERATION with rich parent context
  Answer: "Physical damage is not covered [PARENT CHUNK 1]. 
           The warranty only covers manufacturing defects [PARENT CHUNK 1]."

WHY THIS WORKS:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Small child chunks → High retrieval PRECISION
                     (specific match to query)
Large parent chunks → High generation QUALITY
                      (LLM has full context)

Without hierarchy:
  Large chunks → Low retrieval precision (too generic)
  Small chunks → Low generation quality (missing context)
```
